title: Radio building blocks
idea: A radio is a handful of blocks, each with one job. The exam names the job and asks for the block.

items: A receiver's ability to detect a signal (a weak one)
A receiver's ability to pick one signal out of many
Generates a signal at a specific frequency
The variable frequency oscillator: sets the receive and transmit frequency
Converts a signal from one frequency to another
Converts a transceiver's RF input and output to another band
Combining speech with an RF carrier

pairs: Picks one signal out of many
Generates a signal at one frequency
Moves a signal to another frequency
Moves a whole rig to another band
Puts speech on an RF carrier

compare.how: Can it hear the signal at all?
Can it pick one signal out from its neighbors?
Changes a transceiver's RF in and out to another band.

traps.why: Selectivity is separating signals. Detecting a signal is sensitivity.
Sensitivity is detecting a signal. Telling signals apart is selectivity.
An amplifier makes a signal stronger at the same frequency. A mixer moves it to another frequency.
Moving a transceiver's RF to another band is a transverter.
An oscillator makes the carrier. Putting speech onto it is modulation.

traps.wrong: Inject a variable frequency to allow CW reception
traps.why: The VFO's job is simpler: it sets the receive and transmit frequency.
